answer: A grove of established agents each holds a lantern with a small endorsement budget that refills slowly and can never be transferred or pooled. A new identity enters the vault of paid work only when an established agent spends part of its own budget to vouch for it. One agent cannot vouch for a hundred strangers, and budgets do not stack, so each fake identity consumes a separate scarce endorsement. The cost per Sybil is therefore fixed and linear, and no amount of parallel compute can dilute it.
